title: Malaysia Declares Haze Emergency in Sarawak's Serian District as API Hits 521
detail: Malaysia's King consented to declare a state of emergency for the Serian district of Sarawak on Sept 4 after the Air Pollutant Index hit 521 — above the API-500 threshold Deputy Premier Douglas Uggah Embas had earlier flagged as the trigger for mandatory closures — while state capital Kuching registered a hazardous 311. The emergency covers Serian, an agricultural town of roughly 90,000 near the Kalimantan border, with 647 schools shut across Sarawak from Monday through at least the following week (schools close automatically once the API exceeds 200). Authorities launched a three-day cloud-seeding operation and began distributing clean drinking water as respiratory complaints surged and residents rushed to buy haze-rated masks. Indonesia's Forestry Ministry detected 717 hotspots nationwide since Aug 1, with Kalimantan among the worst-hit provinces feeding the smoke drifting into Sarawak — an escalation from the hazardous-but-pre-emergency API readings (up to 408) recorded in the same areas on Sept 1.

media.caption: Haze blankets Sarawak as Malaysia declares an emergency in Serian district

title: Singapore's 24-Hour PSI Enters Unhealthy Range for First Time Since 2023 as Haze Spreads
detail: Singapore's 24-hour Pollutant Standards Index (PSI) crossed into the unhealthy range (101-200) at 7am on Sept. 4, reaching 105 by 10am in the central region — the first unhealthy reading since October 2023. The National Environment Agency (NEA) said dry weather had increased hotspot activity and smoke haze from Sumatra and Kalimantan, and activated its Haze Task Force, which will now issue daily haze advisories with 24-hour PSI forecasts. NEA urged residents, especially the elderly, pregnant women, children, and those with chronic heart and lung conditions, to reduce outdoor activity and seek medical attention promptly if symptoms develop. The reading marks the regional haze crisis — already at hazardous levels in Malaysia's Sarawak — spreading to a fourth country after Indonesia, Malaysia, and the Philippines.

media.caption: Singapore's PSI enters the unhealthy range for the first time since 2023 as regional haze spreads

title: Panama Canal Postpones Further Neopanamax Draft Cut as El Niño Drought Watch Continues
detail: The Panama Canal Authority (ACP) announced on Sept. 4 that it will postpone a scheduled reduction of the Neopanamax locks' maximum draft from 48.0 feet (14.63m) to 47.5 feet (14.48m) that had been due to take effect Oct. 1, maintaining the current limit for now. The ACP said the decision followed its latest review of Gatun Lake water levels and weather projections, aiming to give shipping customers operational continuity while preserving freshwater reserves. Canal Administrator Ricaurte Vásquez had previously warned the intensifying El Niño could bring 'a very, very low level of precipitation' lasting roughly eight months. The postponement does not affect the daily transit-slot cuts (Neopanamax to 9/day, Panamax to 25/day, falling further to 23/day on Sept. 15) that took effect Sept. 3.

media.caption: The Panama Canal Authority postpones a further Neopanamax draft cut amid El Niño drought monitoring
